## Stripe (https://stripe.com)

### Company Overview
Stripe describes itself as “financial infrastructure to grow your revenue,” providing online and in-person payment processing plus a broader suite of APIs and no-code tools for billing, payouts, fraud prevention, issuing, tax, and more. On its homepage, Stripe cites scale metrics including **$1.4T in payments volume processed in 2024**, **135+ currencies and payment methods supported**, **99.999% historical uptime**, and **200M+ active subscriptions** managed via Stripe Billing.

### Positioning & Messaging
- Core headline/value prop: **“Financial infrastructure to grow your revenue.”**
- Expanded promise: **“Accept payments, offer financial services, and implement custom revenue models—from your first transaction to your billionth.”**
- Targets a wide range: startups → enterprises; highlights “50% of Fortune 100 companies have used Stripe…” (homepage).
- Messaging emphasizes modularity (“designed to work individually or together”), global reach, reliability, and modern developer experience.

- For complete fees and product-specific pricing (e.g., Billing, Connect, Terminal, Radar, Tax, Issuing), Stripe points users to the centralized pricing experience at **https://stripe.com/pricing**.

Adyen highlights unified commerce themes—helping enterprises accept payments across channels, manage risk, and use a single platform/infrastructure.

### Positioning & Messaging

## Summary & Recommendations
Stripe’s website emphasizes breadth, developer experience, and measurable scale (notably **$1.4T processed in 2024** and **99.999% historical uptime**), positioning Stripe as a flexible platform from early-stage startups through Fortune 100 enterprises. Adyen positions around enterprise ambition and **single-platform infrastructure**, with public pricing that appears to be organized by payment method and region, aligning with complex global commerce needs.

For deeper pricing intelligence, a follow-up crawl should focus on extracting the actual fee tables from both **/pricing** pages (they appear to be rendered in a way that didn’t cleanly convert to markdown in this run). From a competitive standpoint, Stripe’s differentiation leans toward a large modular product surface area and ecosystem (apps/partners), while Adyen’s narrative leans toward unified infrastructure and enterprise-grade operations/licensing.
